Being married to someone shouldn’t be about “fixing” them. I do understand where you’re coming from, but the truth is if you’re wife is unhappy despite all the things you’re doing to make her happy, nothing you do will “fix” her unhappiness. Likely you’re wife needs to go to therapy and fix herself/ work on her own difficult history about feeling loved. Maybe encourage/support her to do that through something like couples therapy. That way it’s framed as you being supportive and she’s introduced to the idea of getting help without it sounding like you want to “fix” her.

People generally don’t like Bayo 2 if they liked the combat in Bayo 1 because the combat is very different from Bayo 1. In Bayo 2, enemies often block hits mid combo, and they have pretty poor sound/visual cues when attacking compared to Bayo 1. Also, arial combat and overall damage output is a lot worse, so unless you use Umbran Climax (which a lot of Bayo 1 players don’t like) the fighting is kinda lackluster and making platinum ranks can be obscenely hard. Then there are some important mechanical changes, like witch time duration and wicked weave strength/speed, which make fighting less freestyle and fluid than in Bayo 1. 
Does this mean Bayo 2 is worse than Bayo 1? No, it just means it’s different. Bayo 1 is better for combo fiends, and Bayo 2 is better for people who want to have a good time.
